C-MUYA-MODEL-SURGERY.Summary: Close the muya model-surgery debt of wave-5 bundle C: the contentState mutates the document model before the external operation that justifies the mutation has confirmed, and nothing undoes the mutation when the operation fails, so a failed image paste or drop leaves a placeholder that was never justified (the loading token, the empty-src token with its FileReader preview entry, or the whole dropped paragraph block) stranded in the document with only a console.error and a TODO comment as acknowledgment, and the bullet-to-task conversion rebuilds the surrounding list through transient wrapper blocks (taskListWrapper, bulletListWrapper) with a manual sibling re-parenting loop instead of a direct structural conversion. This change binds every one of the three insertion sites (insertImageFromPath, the pasteImage bitmap branch, the dragDropCtrl file-drop branch) to the confirmed-or-rolled-back contract: after a failed imageAction the document is byte-identical to the pre-operation state (getMarkdown and the block tree, with no loading-* token, no urlMap residue and no orphaned wrapper), the existing return codes stay exactly what the C-24 callers already consume, and the failure is surfaced as an engine-clean signal (codes and parameters, no prose) that replaces the TODO comment; and it replaces the updateTaskListItem wrapper surgery with a direct conversion that constructs no intermediate list block and provably preserves every mid-list sibling item in order, pinned so the guarantee survives future edits.

Goals.Goal: Confirmed-or-rolled-back insertion on the path branch (F-008, insertImageFromPath). After this.muya.options.imageAction rejects, the document is byte-identical to the pre-operation state: the block tree contains no loading-* token, getMarkdown() returns exactly the pre-operation string, no stateRender.urlMap entry was created, and the cursor sits at a valid pre-operation position; on success nothing changes (token inserted, then rewritten through the existing urlMap/replaceImage flow). The mechanism is the plan's choice between rollback (undo the :177-187 write: restore the block text and cursor captured before insertion) and insert-after-confirm (run imageAction first, insert only on success), but the observable contract above is binding, the return codes are binding and unchanged ('' on handled failure, null on non-image input, the path on success), and the silent failure branch (:192-195) is replaced: the TODO comment goes away and every imageAction rejection surfaces as an engine-clean failure signal (an eventCenter dispatch under the existing muya-* event convention or a dedicated options callback, carrying parameters only: the identifier and the raw error, never prose) so the host can map it to a user-facing notice through its existing notify channel.

Confirmed-or-rolled-back insertion on the bitmap and drop branches (F-008, pasteImage and dragDropCtrl). The pasteImage bitmap branch (:231-288) honors the same contract: after an imageAction rejection the empty-src token, the urlMap id entry and any ag-empty-image/ag-image-success wrapper class residue are gone and getMarkdown() is byte-identical, with the return contract unchanged (the file value on success, null on failure and on no-file input). The dragDropCtrl file branch (:144-193) honors it for whole-block insertion: after an imageAction rejection the inserted paragraph block is removed and the document is byte-identical, the dropAnchor/cursor state is restored, and the same engine-clean failure signal fires; the web-link drop branch (:107-142) is not touched (it inserts a remote-URL image with no external operation to confirm).

Direct task conversion without transient wrappers (F-011). updateTaskListItem converts the target item to a task item without constructing intermediate wrapper blocks: no taskListWrapper or bulletListWrapper is created and discarded on the conversion path, the preceding and following siblings are not walked through a remove-and-reinsert loop, and the delivered block-tree outcome is today's outcome (the converting item is an input-bearing task li, the siblings keep their types and their relative order, and the mixed list is represented exactly as today, including the current sibling-list split shape recorded in the Problem). Every sibling item survives every conversion branch: only-child, first-child, last-child and mid-list, pinned by test so the guarantee is regression-proof rather than incidental. This goal is a behavior-preserving refactor of the construction path; no behavioral change of the converted document is claimed, and the pins are recorded honestly as meaningful-proof guards (green on the pre-change tree), not red-first.

Governance: the file-local markup of the touched muya files is updated in the same bundle as the code (pasteCtrl.js updates its existing MODULE_CONTRACT/CHANGE_SUMMARY/VERSION for the rolled-back insertion contract; updateCtrl.js and dragDropCtrl.js, which carry no file-local contract header on this baseline, gain the standard START_MODULE_CONTRACT/START_MODULE_MAP headers documenting the divergence from the upstream algorithm under the local divergence policy, exactly as the other governed muya files already do); .grace/graph/runtime.xml gains the M-012 SummaryDelta and .grace/verification/runtime.xml gains the V-M-012 scenario entries naming the new tests; no version, release, tag or publication is authorized by this specification.
